answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every account to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it can place jobs or earn reputation. If an account is caught double-claiming work or colluding in a verified dispute, the protocol destroys part of that bond and distributes the loss to harmed users. Creating a hundred identities therefore means funding a hundred bonds, not merely generating usernames; the attacker must tie up capital and risk losing it. Whether the market is gale-swept, shale-built, or a quiet harbor, the same stake requirement applies.
